name: Churchill Memorials — Request a Quote → GoHighLevel field map
description: Maps fields from the WooCommerce 'Request a Quote' email (sender no-reply@churchillmemorials.co.uk, subject '[Request a quote]') to GoHighLevel Contact and Opportunity records.

preferred_source.why: Same request lands as a structured WooCommerce order — no HTML/regex parsing of the notification email. Map from here where possible; fall back to the email 'source'/'parse_rules' only when the order is not retrievable.

order_meta._raq_status: lifecycle flag (new, ...) — usable for dedupe / unprocessed filtering
order_meta._raq_request: structured object; each field is { id, type, label, value }

field_map.options: order.line_items[0].meta_data[] — keys: 'Pick A Memorial Colour', 'Pick Lettering Colour', 'Flower Container', 'Photo Plaque', 'Garden Kerbset', 'Inscription', 'overall-height'

value_cleanup.html_entities: Line-item option values contain entities: decode ' '->space, '£'->'£'.
value_cleanup.overage_token: Strip the trailing '+ £<amount>' price token from option/inscription values (e.g. 'Gold  +£0.00' -> 'Gold'; inscription '... +£24.50' -> drop the '+£24.50').

preferred_source.note: order_type, occasion and deceased_name are still DERIVED per 'derived_fields' below — the REST source removes parsing work, not the inference gaps in 'known_gaps'.
preferred_source.validated_against: Live orders #8649-#8675 via the 'CM: Lookup WooCommerce Orders' Make tool (e.g. #8675 Susan GIBNEY / sgibney85@gmail.com, SKU 16019-01, £1399.50).

parse_rules.product_name: First product row, text before the '(#SKU)' token
parse_rules.options: Each 'Label: Value + £ amount' line under the product row (Memorial Colour, Lettering Colour, Flower Container, Photo Plaque, Garden Kerbset, Choose infill, etc.)
parse_rules.inscription: Text after 'Inscription:' up to the '+ £' charge token; preserve line breaks
parse_rules.customer_message: Text under "Customer's message" block (optional; absent on many requests)
parse_rules.order_value: Numeric value after 'Total:' — strip '£' and thousands separators
parse_rules.grave_location: After 'Grave Location :' (free text — postcode, address, or cemetery name; often empty)

order_type.note: If a Garden Kerbset add-on is present on a headstone, append ' + Garden Kerbset' or tag separately.

occasion.note: The website form does NOT capture an explicit occasion. This is inferred from the inscription text and should be treated as a best-guess default that the team can correct in GHL.

deceased_name.rule: Name line following 'In loving memory of' / 'In memory of' if present; else blank. The requester (Contact) is frequently NOT the deceased.

custom_fields.label: Additional Notes
custom_fields.from: concat: customer_message + all remaining product options

upsert_strategy.contact: Upsert on email (fallback phone). Do not overwrite non-empty existing standard fields.
upsert_strategy.opportunity: Create one opportunity per quote request; dedupe on quote_request_number to avoid duplicates on retries.

known_gaps: Website form has no explicit 'Cemetery' field — 'Grave Location' is free text (postcode / address / cemetery name / blank) and needs normalisation before it is a reliable cemetery value.
Website form has no 'Occasion' field — occasion is inferred from the inscription and defaults to 'Memorial (bereavement)'.
Last Name is sometimes empty (e.g. Req #9982). Opportunity naming must tolerate a missing last name.
Order value is the customer-configured WooCommerce total and is a starting figure only — it is NOT the final quoted price and excludes any cemetery permit fee.
